# govengers/postgrestest

> Fast PostgreSQL for Go tests: postgrestest.New(&Options{Migrate, Fingerprint}) returns a Server whose Pool(t) / Database(t) give every test its own database, copied (CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE) from a template built once by Migrate and dropped after the test; an embedded PostgreSQL 18 per test binary on a Unix socket (binaries unpacked once per machine with the system tar into ~/.embedded-postgres-go/postgrestest), one server per test run through the launcher cmd/postgrestest, or an external server from POSTGRESTEST_URL; orphaned servers of dead processes swept, live ones of other checkouts untouched; every test input stable so the Go test cache keeps hitting.

- Module: `github.com/govengers/postgrestest`, Go 1.26, Apache 2.0. Dependencies: pgx v5, embedded-postgres.
- Package `postgrestest`: New, Options (Migrate, Fingerprint), Server (Database, Pool, Main, Close, WithTemplate), Statements, FingerprintFS, EnvironmentVariable (`POSTGRESTEST_URL`), ErrClosed, TestingM.
- Command `cmd/postgrestest command...`: one server for the run, `POSTGRESTEST_URL` set for the command, exit status passed through.
- Standards: govengers/standards, `library` profile.
- Rules of thumb: one Server per test package in a package variable, `TestMain` is `goleak.VerifyTestMain(postgres.Main(m))`; Migrate must close every connection it opens; Fingerprint = the migration SQL or FingerprintFS(embed.FS); ALTER DATABASE SET is not copied to test databases; scope pg_locks/pg_stat_activity polls to current_database(); start the launcher the same way every time (go run changes PATH, a test cache input).
